objective: Implement an Integration-owned append-only semantic-action correlation ledger that reconstructs one stable record per run_id and action_id across dispatch, transport attempts, MCU acknowledgement or fault, Motion ActionResult evidence, persisted WorldEvent identity, and verification lookup, while reusing the existing SQLiteEventStore and changing no shared interface or owning runtime module.
decision_supported: Can the repository replay and structurally join one SemanticAction across Agent dispatch, MCU transport, Motion evidence, WorldEvent persistence and verification lookup without parsing free-form messages, inventing physical-success evidence, or creating a second event store?
outputs: An Integration-owned strict correlation ledger keyed by run_id and action_id.
An append-only projection reconstructed from the existing WorldEventStore rather than a second mutable store.
Structured correlation of task_id, action_id, command_id, frame_id, retry_count, result_id, WorldEvent event_id, evidence references and verification identity.
Documented action-level and run-level fault ownership, retry semantics and non-causation boundary.
Focused unit and end-to-end integration evidence.
acceptance: Recording one contract-valid SemanticAction dispatch creates exactly one stable logical correlation record keyed by run_id and action_id. Repeating the identical dispatch is idempotent, while conflicting task, action or payload reuse fails closed. Test: test_dispatch_creates_one_stable_record.

A new MCU logical request binds one command_id to exactly one run_id and action_id. Deliberate retries preserve command_id and command semantics while distinct frame_id and retry_count values remain visible as separate transport attempts. Test: test_transport_retries_preserve_identity_and_distinguish_attempts.

Structured projection fields join task_id, action_id, command_id, frame_id, result_id, WorldEvent event_id, evidence references and verification identity without parsing logs or free-form messages. Test: test_structured_ids_join_without_message_parsing.

An acknowledgement, ActionResult, Motion evidence reference or WorldEvent whose run_id, action_id, command_id or result identity conflicts with its existing binding is rejected before append. A duplicate or late result cannot attach to a different action or replace a terminal binding. Tests: test_cross_run_or_action_rebinding_fails_closed and test_duplicate_and_late_results_cannot_rebind.

STOP command and stop_ack entries bind to their explicit STOP action when command correlation exists. Watchdog or link-loss telemetry without command_id binds to the sole explicit active action only when that scope is unambiguous; otherwise it is recorded as an explicit run-level cause and never guessed. Test: test_stop_and_watchdog_fault_scope_is_explicit.

Ledger entries are persisted through the existing SQLiteEventStore as append-only WorldEvents. Closing and reopening the database reconstructs an equal immutable projection in sequence order, and no second table or event store is introduced. Test: test_reopen_replays_identical_record.

Missing, blank, malformed, cross-run or internally inconsistent correlation fields fail before SQLite insertion and before reducer-visible state mutation. Event counts and deterministic WorldState output remain unchanged after rejection. Test: test_malformed_correlation_fails_before_append_or_reduction.

The end-to-end integration test uses the actual Issue #59 ExecutionController, shared SemanticAction, ActionResult and McuFrame contracts, actual Motion ExecutionEvent, Issue #56 MotionEvidenceAdapter, SQLiteEventStore, WorldEvent replay and World Model verifier lookup. Test: test_observe_plan_dispatch_mcu_motion_world_event_verification_lookup.

Verification lookup remains traceability only. Action execution evidence and Observation-backed VerificationResult evidence remain separate, and the ledger exposes no physical-execution, task-completion or causal-success claim. Test: test_ledger_separates_execution_and_verification_evidence.
The final diff relative to the approved combined #47 and #59 base contains only the five allowed paths, and every required repository check passes.

Full make test, contract, scenario, context, demo-scripted and make check output.
Task Packet boundary output relative to the approved combined dependency base.

risks_and_fallbacks: Issue #52 remains open, so the end-to-end test can use actual contract and persistence types but still requires an injected fake semantic dispatch producer; this is not physical Motion evidence.
MCU telemetry has no command_id and cannot confirm a command. The bounded fallback is explicit run-level fault scope whenever one active action cannot be proven.
Protocol v1 has no on-wire boot or session epoch. The ledger must consume the transport owner's accepted or late classification and must not independently reinterpret raw frames across restart.
Verification evidence is expected to remain Observation-backed after Issue #150. The ledger joins verification by structured run_id and task_id while preserving separate evidence lists.
If production producers need to emit a new shared ledger envelope, stop and open an interfaces task using the three-owner process.
Rollback consists of removing the Integration-owned correlation module, documentation and its tests; existing Agent Runtime, Motion, MCU and World Model behavior remains unchanged.
